results.name: Algebra.IsEffective
results.source_text:
/-- For an `R`-algebra `S`, this asserts that the maps `algebraMap : R → S` and
`includeLeftSubRight R S : S → S ⊗[R] S` form an exact pair.
When `R` and `S` are commutative rings, this is true if and only if the inclusion
`im (algebraMap : R → S) → S` is an effective monomorphism in the category of commutative rings. -/
def IsEffective : Prop :=
  Function.Exact (Algebra.linearMap R S) (TensorProduct.includeLeftSubRight R S)
results.docstring:
For an `R`-algebra `S`, this asserts that the maps `algebraMap : R → S` and
`includeLeftSubRight R S : S → S ⊗[R] S` form an exact pair.
When `R` and `S` are commutative rings, this is true if and only if the inclusion
`im (algebraMap : R → S) → S` is an effective monomorphism in the category of commutative rings.

results.name: Ordnode.Valid'
results.source_text:
/-- The validity predicate for an `Ordnode` subtree. This asserts that the `size` fields are
correct, the tree is balanced, and the elements of the tree are organized according to the
ordering. This version of `Valid` also puts all elements in the tree in the interval `(lo, hi)`. -/
structure Valid' (lo : WithBot α) (t : Ordnode α) (hi : WithTop α) : Prop where
  ord : t.Bounded lo hi
  sz : t.Sized
  bal : t.Balanced
results.docstring:
The validity predicate for an `Ordnode` subtree. This asserts that the `size` fields are
correct, the tree is balanced, and the elements of the tree are organized according to the
ordering. This version of `Valid` also puts all elements in the tree in the interval `(lo, hi)`.

results.name: Ordnode.Valid

/-- The validity predicate for an `Ordnode` subtree. This asserts that the `size` fields are
correct, the tree is balanced, and the elements of the tree are organized according to the

def Valid (t : Ordnode α) : Prop :=

results.name: ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.measurable_kernel_prodMk_left'
results.source_text:
theorem measurable_kernel_prodMk_left' [IsSFiniteKernel η] {s : Set (β × γ)} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (a : α) : Measurable fun b => η (a, b) (Prod.mk b ⁻¹' s) := by
  have (b : _) : Prod.mk b ⁻¹' s = {c | ((a, b), c) ∈ {p : (α × β) × γ | (p.1.2, p.2) ∈ s}} := rfl
  simp_rw [this]
  refine (measurable_kernel_prodMk_left ?_).comp measurable_prodMk_left
  exact (measurable_fst.snd.prodMk measurable_snd) hs

results.name: btw_cyclic
results.source_text:
/-- The order of the `↔` has been chosen so that `rw [btw_cyclic]` cycles to the right while
`rw [← btw_cyclic]` cycles to the left (thus following the prepended arrow). -/
theorem btw_cyclic {a b c : α} : btw a b c ↔ btw c a b :=
  ⟨btw_cyclic_right, btw_cyclic_left⟩
results.docstring:
The order of the `↔` has been chosen so that `rw [btw_cyclic]` cycles to the right while
`rw [← btw_cyclic]` cycles to the left (thus following the prepended arrow).

results.name: Rand.next
results.source_text:
/-- Generate a random `Nat`. -/
def next [RandomGen g] [Monad m] : RandGT g m Nat := do
  let rng := (← get).down
  let (res, new) := RandomGen.next rng
  set (ULift.up new)
  pure res

results.name: Mathlib.Tactic.Translate.insertTranslationChecked
results.source_text:
/-- A version of `insertTranslation` that checks whether the translation is valid, and only
inserts the translation if it is valid. -/
def insertTranslationChecked (t : TranslateData) (src tgt : Name) (cfg : Config) : CoreM Unit := do
  let (reorder, relevantArg) ←
    try
      checkExistingType t src tgt cfg (lint := false) |>.run'
    catch ex =>
      Linter.logLintIf linter.translate.warnInvalid cfg.ref m!"\
        @[{t.attrName}] failed to add a translation from `{.ofConstName src}` to \
        `{.ofConstName tgt}`.\nPlease silence this warning and add a translation manually. \
        Error:\n\n{ex.toMessageData}"
      return
  insertTranslation t src tgt reorder relevantArg cfg.ref
results.docstring:
A version of `insertTranslation` that checks whether the translation is valid, and only
inserts the translation if it is valid.

results.name: Filter.generate
results.source_text:
/-- `generate g` is the largest filter containing the sets `g`. -/
def generate (g : Set (Set α)) : Filter α where
  sets := {s | GenerateSets g s}
  univ_sets := GenerateSets.univ
  sets_of_superset := GenerateSets.superset
  inter_sets := GenerateSets.inter
results.docstring: `generate g` is the largest filter containing the sets `g`.

results.name: Physlib.RemarkInfo.getRemarkInfo
results.source_text:
/-- Gets the remarkInfo from a name corresponding to a remark.. -/
meta def RemarkInfo.getRemarkInfo (n : Name) : m RemarkInfo := do
  let allRemarks ← allRemarkInfo
  match allRemarks.find? fun r => r.toFullName == n with
  | some r => return r
  | none => throwError s!"No remark named {n}"
results.docstring: Gets the remarkInfo from a name corresponding to a remark..
